scenario.summary: Attackers used adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) relays to capture Microsoft 365 session tokens, which were then replayed from a centralized hosting provider (1337 Services GmbH) in a large-scale token-spraying campaign. Once authenticated, the actors registered rogue Entra ID devices and modified MFA methods to ensure persistent access before deploying hidden inbox rules to facilitate business email compromise and payroll fraud.

meta.rationale: Prioritize accounts with Global Administrator roles or finance department associations, as the report highlights these as primary targets for rogue device registration and payroll fraud.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has replayed session tokens stolen through AiTM relays to register rogue devices and establish persistent MFA methods in the victim tenant.

blind_spots.risk: Without advanced auditing, granular MFA tampering events such as specific factor labels (e.g., iPhone 13) may be missing, leaving only generic success records.
blind_spots.question: whether the specific MFA registration event can be attributed to the relay IP
blind_spots.requires: M365 Unified Audit Log (UAL) with Advanced Auditing enabled

blind_spots.risk: Replayed tokens inherit the MFA status of the original session; if telemetry cannot distinguish the relay IP from the replay IP within the same session context, the replay may appear as a legitimate resumption.
blind_spots.question: whether existing CA policies were applied to the replayed session

hunt.name: Entra ID Identity Hijack and Persistence
hunt.description: This hunt tracks a campaign pairing AiTM phishing with token replay to bypass MFA and secure directory persistence. It follows a phased flow: the first phase identifies potentially hijacked sessions by examining successful MFA attempts from known relay infrastructure and replayed activity using scripted user agents. The second phase correlates these sessions with directory persistence indicators, specifically rogue Entra-joined devices and unauthorized MFA method tampering. This approach ensures that directory-level changes are evaluated in the context of high-probability session compromises.

config.instructions: Revoke all active sessions and refresh tokens for the compromised accounts. Temporarily disable account access pending a full MFA reset and password rotation.

config.instructions: Delete rogue devices matching the DESKTOP-[HEX8] naming convention from the tenant directory. Audit the registered MFA methods for the affected users in the Entra portal and remove any factors not explicitly confirmed by the user.
